shortlist.label: Traumatic spinal cord injury
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with quadriplegia and spinal cord compression after a fall

shortlist.label: Cervical spine fracture-dislocation
shortlist.why_kept: MRI showed disruptions at C4 and C5 with spinal cord compression and anterolisthesis

shortlist.label: Spinal cord contusion
shortlist.why_kept: Reduced diffusion in spinal cord white matter on DWI suggests traumatic injury

shortlist.label: Spinal epidural hematoma
shortlist.why_kept: Hypointense signal of central gray matter on DWI could indicate hemorrhage

shortlist.label: Cervical spondylotic myelopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's age and symptoms suggest possible underlying cervical spondylosis

raw.rationale: The patient's history of falling out of bed, quadriplegia, urinary and stool incontinence, and hypothermia, combined with MRI findings of spinal cord compression and reduced diffusion in spinal cord white matter, are consistent with a traumatic spinal cord injury.

rejected.label: Cervical spine fracture-dislocation
rejected.why: While the patient has spinal cord compression at C4 and C5 with anterolisthesis, this is a consequence of the injury rather than the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Spinal cord contusion
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are more consistent with a traumatic spinal cord injury, which can include contusion, rather than contusion being the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Spinal epidural hematoma
rejected.why: There is no mention of a hematoma on the MRI findings, making this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Cervical spondylotic myelopathy
rejected.why: The patient's acute presentation and history of trauma are not consistent with this chronic condition.
